insight.title: The Bike Company That Printed TVs to Stop Shipping Damage
insight.subtitle: How a simple packaging change saved a startup from logistical bankruptcy.

sections.text: VanMoof was shipping expensive electric bikes globally, but 25% arrived damaged. Couriers treated the large boxes like scrap metal, despite "Fragile" stickers. The replacement costs were nearly bankrupting the startup.
The founders realized couriers simply didn't value bicycles. They noticed their boxes were the same size as large TVs, so they printed a massive television image on every shipping box.
The bikes inside remained the same, but the handling changed instantly. Shipping damage plummeted by 80%. Couriers who once tossed boxes now carried them with delicate, two-handed care.
We protect what we think we cannot afford to break.
